stories.title: Solana cuts block time to 350 milliseconds as first governance vote nears
stories.summary: Solana reduced its slot time to 350 milliseconds, a change meant to speed up block production on the network. Separately, Solana's first-ever governance vote is approaching, but a live quorum display showing 60% appears to have a bug, per CryptoSlate.
stories.whyItMatters: Faster block times affect Solana's competitiveness against other chains, and a buggy quorum display raises questions about the reliability of the network's first governance process.
whatToWatch: Result of Solana's first governance vote
Whether the quorum display error gets fixed or explained
Stability of the network after the 350ms slot time change
questions: What does the governance vote actually decide?
Is the quorum bug just a display issue, or does it affect real vote counts?

sources.title: Solana’s first governance vote nears with a live 60% quorum display error

stories.title: Bitcoin surges 25% toward $80,000 as Treasury bond buyback tweak lifts risk appetite
stories.summary: Bitcoin jumped about 25% in a matter of days, nearing $80,000, a rally CoinDesk links to a tweak in the US Treasury's bond buyback program. Separately, the Treasury set a deadline for offshore stablecoin issuers to keep their access to US customers, per CryptoSlate.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally ties bitcoin's price to macro liquidity policy rather than crypto-specific news, while the stablecoin deadline signals tighter US enforcement on offshore issuers.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin holds its gains near $80,000
The Treasury's stablecoin deadline and which issuers must comply
questions: What exactly changed in the Treasury buyback program?
Which offshore stablecoin issuers are affected by the deadline?

sources.title: Treasury just put a deadline on offshore stablecoins’ access to US customers
How a Treasury buyback tweak helped bitcoin surge 25% to nearly $80,000 in days

stories.title: SEC proposes $75 million raise pathway that lets tokens later exit securities status
stories.summary: The SEC has proposed a rule that would let crypto projects raise up to $75 million and later end the token's classification as a security, according to CryptoSlate. Few other details of the proposal have surfaced yet.
stories.whyItMatters: A defined path for tokens to exit securities status would resolve years of regulatory uncertainty and could reshape how new projects structure token sales.
whatToWatch: Formal proposed rule text and comment period
Industry and issuer reaction to the plan
questions: What conditions would a token need to meet to end its securities status?
Would this apply to tokens already sold under securities rules?

stories.title: EU regulators eye DeFi vaults under MiCA, but enforcement won't be easy
stories.summary: Cointelegraph reports that the EU's MiCA framework is turning attention to DeFi vaults, the automated smart-contract products that pool and manage user funds. Applying licensing rules built for centralized firms to decentralized, code-based systems poses real practical problems.
stories.whyItMatters: How MiCA treats DeFi vaults will determine whether decentralized protocols can keep serving EU users or face the same compliance load as centralized exchanges.
whatToWatch: Formal MiCA guidance or enforcement targeting DeFi vaults
Whether major protocols restrict EU access in response
questions: Who would be held liable for a vault with no central operator?
Which DeFi products count as vaults under the rule?

sources.title: MiCA is coming for DeFi vaults, but regulation will be difficult

stories.title: Crypto's week: short squeeze pummels bears, X eyes stablecoin payouts for creators
stories.summary: CoinDesk's weekly roundup covers a squeeze-led rally that hit bitcoin and ether short-sellers hard this week, plus reports that Elon Musk's X wants to pay creators using stablecoins. The roundup groups five stories from the week's crypto markets and business news.
stories.whyItMatters: A short squeeze can push prices further than fundamentals justify, while X adopting stablecoin payouts would be a notable use case for the technology beyond trading.
whatToWatch: Whether the rally holds once short positions are cleared out
Any official rollout details from X on stablecoin payments
questions: How much of the rally was short-covering versus new demand?
Which stablecoin would X actually use, and where?

stories.title: Bitcoin nears $80,000 as ETF buying support fades into the weekend
stories.summary: Bitcoin approached $80,000, but CryptoSlate notes the buying support from spot ETFs typically disappears over the weekend since funds don't trade Saturday or Sunday. That leaves weekend price moves more exposed to thinner spot-market trading.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows have become a major driver of bitcoin's price, so a weekend without that support is a real test of whether the current rally has staying power.
whatToWatch: ETF inflow and outflow data when markets reopen Monday
Whether bitcoin holds near $80,000 over the weekend
questions: How much of the recent rally is ETF-driven versus organic spot demand?

sources.title: Bitcoin hits $80,000’s doorstep just as the ETF bid disappears for the weekend

stories.title: Riot's bitcoin rally could free up 1,500 BTC pledged during earlier crash
stories.summary: Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms had pledged 1,825 BTC as collateral after a previous price crash. CryptoSlate reports the recent rally may now let Riot release as much as 1,500 BTC of that pledged collateral.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how mining companies lean on bitcoin holdings as loan collateral, and how price swings directly affect their financial flexibility.
whatToWatch: Confirmation from Riot on any collateral release
Riot's disclosed BTC holdings in upcoming updates
questions: What loan or obligation was the pledged BTC securing?
Would Riot sell freed-up bitcoin or keep holding it?

stories.title: Zcash surges 48% past $800 on Grayscale spot ETF push
stories.summary: Zcash jumped about 48% to trade above $800, a move CoinDesk ties to Grayscale's push for a spot Zcash ETF. The rally has fueled talk of Zcash as a "next bitcoin" candidate, a comparison worth treating with caution.
stories.whyItMatters: A privacy coin drawing ETF interest would mark a notable shift, given regulators' historical wariness toward privacy-focused crypto assets.
whatToWatch: Whether Grayscale formally files for a spot Zcash ETF
Any SEC response to the filing push
questions: Has Grayscale actually filed, or is this speculative positioning?
How much of the price move survives once ETF speculation cools?

stories.title: BitMart considers partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after shutdown
stories.summary: Crypto exchange BitMart, which announced a shutdown weeks ago, is reportedly weighing a partial restart along with payouts to creditors, according to CoinDesk. The situation remains unresolved.
stories.whyItMatters: How BitMart handles creditor claims will be watched as a test case for exchange wind-downs and user fund recovery in crypto.
whatToWatch: A formal announcement on restart timing or payout terms
questions: What caused the original shutdown, and has that issue been fixed?
How much of creditor funds would actually be recovered?

stories.title: The Sandbox halts Base and BNB Chain bridging after exploit
stories.summary: Web3 gaming platform The Sandbox suspended bridging on Base and BNB Chain after an exploit, CoinDesk reports. The pause is a precaution while the incident is investigated.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge exploits remain one of the most common ways funds are stolen in crypto, and this incident shows the risk persists even at established web3 platforms.
whatToWatch: A post-mortem from Sandbox on the exploit's cause and scope
When bridging resumes on Base and BNB Chain
questions: How much was lost in the exploit?
Are user funds affected, or only the bridge contract?

stories.title: Tokenized stocks could repeat Wall Street's 1960s 'paper crisis,' Fairmint CEO warns
stories.summary: The CEO of Fairmint warns that tokenized stocks risk recreating the settlement backlog problems of Wall Street's 1960s "paper crisis," when overwhelmed back-office paperwork forced markets to close early, according to CoinDesk.
stories.whyItMatters: As tokenized equities gain traction, unresolved settlement and infrastructure questions could undercut the argument that blockchain fixes old market plumbing rather than repeating it.
whatToWatch: How tokenized stock platforms address settlement infrastructure as volumes grow
questions: What specific infrastructure gaps is Fairmint's CEO pointing to?
Which tokenized stock platforms are most exposed to this risk?

sources.title: Tokenized stocks risk repeating Wall Street’s 1960s ‘paper crisis,’ Fairmint CEO says

stories.title: AI-driven attacks target Bitcoin software, prompting a new defense effort
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that Bitcoin's core software has become a target for AI-assisted attacks, and a group has formed to counter the threat. The initial report offers limited detail on the specific attack methods or the group's approach.
stories.whyItMatters: If AI tools are lowering the barrier to finding or exploiting flaws in Bitcoin's codebase, that raises the stakes for how the network's core software gets reviewed and secured.
whatToWatch: Further details the group releases on identified attacks or defenses built
questions: What kind of vulnerabilities have AI tools actually found in Bitcoin software?
Who is organizing and funding the defense effort?
